facts.statement: The genus Cyphornis was described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1894.
The only known species within the genus is Cyphornis magnus.
Cyphornis is a genus of prehistoric birds known for having pseudoteeth on their beaks.
facts.quote: Cyphornis is a genus of the prehistoric pseudotooth birds.

facts.statement: The genus is placed in the order Odontopterygiformes due to uncertainty regarding its closest relatives.
facts.quote: are here placed in the order Odontopterygiformes to account for this uncertainty.

facts.statement: The species is known with certainty only from a single, abraded fossil consisting of the proximal part of a left tarsometatarsus.
facts.quote: It is only known with certainty from a single specimen, the rather abraded proximal part of a left tarsometatarsus

facts.statement: The fossil deposits were initially dated to the Eocene but are usually assigned to the Early Miocene.
facts.quote: The deposits from which it originated were initially dated to the Eocene; subsequent authors have usually assigned them to the Early Miocene

facts.statement: At the time of its discovery, Cyphornis was considered the largest known bird capable of flight.
facts.quote: At the time of its discovery, it "probably represent[ed] the largest known bird of flight."

facts.statement: Today, Cyphornis remains one of the largest known flying birds, though not the heaviest.
facts.quote: Even today it is one of the largest (though not heaviest) flying birds known.

facts.statement: The type specimen was found at Carmanah Point on Vancouver Island, Canada, near the entrance to the Juan de Fuca Strait.
facts.quote: found at Carmanah Point on Vancouver Island (Canada), where the Juan de Fuca Strait opens into the Pacific.

facts.statement: Huge pseudotooth wing bone fossils have also been discovered in Oregon.
facts.quote: Some huge pseudotooth wing bone fossils have been found in Oregon.

facts.statement: Fossils found in Washington County and near Mist date from the Eo-Oligocene boundary.
facts.quote: These remains all date from the Eo-Oligocene boundary

facts.statement: Due to its fragmentary nature, Cyphornis was often allied with the enigmatic genus Cladornis.
facts.quote: it was often allied with the enigmatic Cladornis

facts.statement: Modern research generally classifies Cladornis as a terrestrial bird rather than a seabird.
facts.quote: Today however, Cladornis is more generally held to be a terrestrial bird rather than a seabird.

facts.statement: Cyphornis was originally separated into the family Cyphornithidae along with Palaeochenoides mioceanus and Tympanonesiotes wetmorei.
facts.quote: Cyphornis was early on separated in a family Cyphornithidae together with Palaeochenoides mioceanus and eventually also Tympanonesiotes wetmorei

facts.statement: The family Cyphornithidae is almost certainly a junior synonym of the family Pelagornithidae.
facts.quote: Cyphornithidae would almost certainly be a junior synonym of Pelagornithidae

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Cyphornis is the family Pelagornithidae.
Cyphornis lived during the Rupelian to Chattian stages, approximately 33.9 to 23.04 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Chattian (33.9 to 23.04 million years ago)
